governance: CANDIDATES ONLY — discovery is not trust. No row here is an active capability; each must pass the seeder's gap/lift screen, then human/eval gates, before any promotion. Source URLs are as reported; license/verify_note flags carried verbatim. serves_truth=false for everything downstream. Scope: tools that PARSE, INDEX, VECTORIZE, EXPLAIN, or MAP source-code repositories so an agent/developer can understand an unfamiliar codebase. Generic LangChain tool catalogs, scraping, devops/database servers, and non-code research are out of scope (covered by sibling feeds).

candidates.intent: Generate, maintain, and update repository-level Markdown documentation by parsing code structure and inter-object call relationships, triggered on git commits.
candidates.input_contract: a target repository path plus an LLM config and prompt template
candidates.output_contract: per-object Markdown docs reflecting structure and bidirectional invocation relationships, kept in sync with the code
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot walk a whole repo, build a global object/call-graph view, or detect git changes — and exceeds its context window on a 270k-LOC codebase.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds AST-based structure analysis, bidirectional call-graph identification, git change detection, and pre-commit hooks so docs stay current; the LLM only writes prose over the parsed structure.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via repo fetch: Apache-2.0, Python 97%, EMNLP 2024 demo paper (arXiv 2402.16667). AST/call-graph extraction is deterministic; the documentation prose is LLM-generated (model-dependent), hence the moderate ceiling.

candidates.intent: Recursively scan a project, chunk files, and generate vector embeddings into a local DB so a coding LLM can do repository-aware semantic retrieval (with a Neovim plugin and MCP server mode).
candidates.input_contract: a project directory plus an embedding backend and query
candidates.output_contract: semantically relevant code chunks retrieved from the vector DB for prompt augmentation
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no persistent index of a repo, cannot recall code outside its context window, and cannot do semantic retrieval over a large codebase.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Chromadb-backed embeddings with tree-sitter-aware chunking, a CLI, a Neovim plugin, and MCP-server retrieval so the model gets only relevant chunks on demand.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via repo fetch: MIT, Python 74.5% + Lua 25.4% (Neovim plugin), Chromadb vector store, MCP server support confirmed. Tree-sitter semantic chunking noted as in-progress in TODOs; embedding similarity is deterministic given a fixed model.

candidates.intent: Generate a plain-English structured explanation (EXPLAIN.md) of an unfamiliar codebase by first extracting deterministic project signals, then optionally summarizing with an LLM.
candidates.input_contract: a public GitHub repo URL or local path plus a mode (quick/simple/detailed/tech-stack) and optional LLM provider
candidates.output_contract: a structured architectural summary (EXPLAIN.md) grounded in configs, entrypoints, manifests, dependency graph, and file structure
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM guesses about a repo from the README alone, hallucinating architecture it cannot verify; it has no repo access and no deterministic signal extraction.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds 'signals first, LLM second': deterministic extraction of stack/entrypoints/manifests/structure (tech-stack mode needs NO LLM), feeding vetted signals to a pluggable LLM provider for grounded prose.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via repo fetch + site: MIT, Python 49% + TypeScript 48% (Python CLI is reference, Node CLI has parity); pluggable providers (Gemini/OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic/Groq/OpenRouter). Stack-detection path is fully deterministic; explanation prose is LLM-dependent.

candidates.intent: Clone a GitHub repo, chunk and embed it, and build a LangChain QA retriever so a developer can chat with the code in natural language.
candidates.input_contract: a GitHub repo URL plus an embedding/LLM key and a natural-language question
candidates.output_contract: natural-language answers grounded in retrieved code chunks via a QA retriever
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot clone a repo, persist embeddings, or retrieve relevant code beyond its context window to answer questions about an unfamiliar codebase.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a clone -> chunk -> embed -> Deeplake vector store -> LangChain QA-retriever pipeline so the model answers over retrieved code with citations.
candidates.verify_note: BEST EXACT MATCH for the user's 'AI-Code-Explainer (LangChain GitHub-code chunk+embed+chat)': no repo is literally named 'AI-Code-Explainer'; this MIT/Python LangChain+Deeplake repo matches the described behavior. ArchAI-Labs/code_explainer and soos3d/chat-with-repo-langchain-openai are close alternatives (recorded separately).

candidates.intent: Automatically analyze, document, and visualize a codebase using LangChain document loaders plus CrewAI-orchestrated agents over a Qdrant vector store.
candidates.input_contract: a codebase plus an embedding model and LLM config
candidates.output_contract: generated documentation and a holistic codebase view with configurable context chunk sizes
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no document loaders for many language files, no token-budget-aware chunking, and no vector store to scale documentation across a large repo.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds LangChain loaders, tiktoken-based chunk sizing, Qdrant vector modes, code-capable embeddings (jina-embeddings-v2-base-code), and CrewAI agent orchestration for end-to-end doc generation.
candidates.verify_note: Alternative reading of 'AI-Code-Explainer'. Confirmed via search to use LangChain + CrewAI + Qdrant + jina code embeddings; SPDX license not confirmed — verify LICENSE on the repo before relying.

candidates.intent: Convert any Git repository into a single prompt-friendly text digest (replace 'hub' with 'ingest' in a GitHub URL), with file filtering optimized for LLM input.
candidates.input_contract: a GitHub repo URL or local path plus include/exclude patterns and an optional access token
candidates.output_contract: a single concatenated, filtered text digest of the codebase with a directory tree and token estimate
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot fetch a repo, walk its tree, or pack filtered file contents into a single coherent prompt-sized blob.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds deterministic repo fetch, gitignore-aware filtering, directory-tree rendering, and token-count estimation to produce one LLM-ready digest (web, CLI, and browser-extension).
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: MIT, hosted at gitingest.com with CLI + Firefox/Chrome extensions; supports private repos via PAT. Pure deterministic packing — no LLM in the digest step.

candidates.intent: Pack an entire repository into a single AI-friendly file (Markdown/XML/JSON/plain text) with include/ignore control and a built-in secret scan.
candidates.input_contract: a repo path or remote URL plus include/ignore patterns and an output format
candidates.output_contract: a single packed file in the chosen format, with token counts and a secret-detection report
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot assemble a whole repo into one structured artifact, count tokens per file, or flag hardcoded secrets before they enter a prompt.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds deterministic, format-selectable repo packing with fine-grained file selection, token accounting, and a security check that flags secrets pre-output.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: MIT, CLI. Outputs Markdown/XML/JSON/plain text. Distinct from gitingest by format control + built-in secret scanning. Also exposes an MCP server in recent versions (confirm on repo).

candidates.intent: Build an automatic, ranked repository map using tree-sitter symbol extraction plus a PageRank-style graph over file dependencies to surface the most-referenced identifiers as compact context.
candidates.input_contract: a git repository plus a token budget for the map
candidates.output_contract: a concise ranked repo map (files, key symbol definitions/references with line numbers and kinds) sized to a token budget
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot fit a large repo in context or know which symbols matter; it has no symbol graph or dependency ranking to select high-signal context.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds tree-sitter ranked-tags extraction (filename/path/line/name/kind) and a graph ranking algorithm (files=nodes, dependency edges) to pick the most-referenced identifiers within a token budget — a deterministic context selector.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + aider.chat repomap writeup: Apache-2.0, Python. The repo-map subsystem (tree-sitter + PageRank) is the in-scope capability; the broader Aider tool is an LLM coding agent. RepoMapper (pdavis68) is a standalone MCP extraction of this map.

candidates.intent: Parse source code into a concrete syntax tree and incrementally update it as the source is edited, for any language with a tree-sitter grammar.
candidates.input_contract: source-code text (or edits) plus a compiled language grammar
candidates.output_contract: a concrete syntax tree queryable by node type, with incremental re-parse on edits
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no exact, error-tolerant parse of code structure; it cannot reliably extract precise spans, scopes, or node types, and it re-reads everything on each edit.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a fast, incremental, language-agnostic parser producing a real CST with a query language — the deterministic substrate most code-RAG/chunking/symbol tools build on.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + tree-sitter.github.io: MIT, written in Rust + C, initial release 2018 (Max Brunsfeld). Foundational primitive for ast-grep, Semgrep, Aider repo-map, claude-context, llama-index code splitters, CodeGraph, etc.

candidates.intent: Search, lint, and rewrite code by matching tree-sitter ASTs using code-like patterns, AST types, and regex across any grammar-supported language.
candidates.input_contract: a pattern/rule (pattern string, AST kind, or YAML rule) plus a target codebase
candidates.output_contract: matched AST nodes with locations and optional structural rewrites
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot reliably find every structural occurrence of a code pattern or perform precise, syntax-aware rewrites without false positives that text/regex search produces.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds tree-sitter-backed structural matching and rewriting with a rule system (patterns + AST kinds + regex), giving deterministic, language-aware code search/refactor.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + ast-grep.github.io: MIT, Rust CLI built on tree-sitter. In scope for repo understanding as a precise structural query engine over the AST.

candidates.intent: Run lightweight static analysis across 35+ languages by matching a generic AST with patterns written in code-like YAML rules.
candidates.input_contract: YAML rules (patterns resembling source) plus a target codebase
candidates.output_contract: rule findings with file/line locations and matched code
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot exhaustively or reproducibly scan a codebase for structural patterns and tends to miss occurrences or invent matches.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds tree-sitter parsing into a generic cross-language AST plus a YAML pattern engine for deterministic, reproducible structural analysis and code-pattern discovery.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: open-source CLI does AST pattern matching across 35+ languages via tree-sitter; license commonly LGPL-2.1 for the OSS engine (Semgrep Pro/AppSec is commercial) — confirm SPDX on LICENSE. In-scope for understanding code structure, not just security.

candidates.intent: Query a codebase as a relational database to find definitions, references, data flows, and complex semantic patterns using the CodeQL query language.
candidates.input_contract: a compiled/extracted CodeQL database for a codebase plus CodeQL queries
candidates.output_contract: query results identifying code locations, paths, and semantic relationships (e.g. taint/data-flow paths)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot perform sound whole-program data-flow or reference analysis; it cannot trace how values propagate across files without a semantic model.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a semantic database + query language enabling precise definition/reference/data-flow queries with depth and precision a model cannot reproduce.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: github/codeql holds the open-source standard query libraries. The CodeQL CLI/engine itself is under a proprietary GitHub license (free for OSS/research, paid for some commercial use) — SPDX 'unknown'; licensing review required before commercial use.

candidates.intent: Generate a tag (index) file of language objects (functions, classes, variables, etc.) found across source files so editors/tools can jump to definitions.
candidates.input_contract: a set of source files plus language/kind options
candidates.output_contract: a tags file mapping symbol name -> file + line + kind
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no persistent symbol index; it cannot reliably enumerate every definition in a repo or map a symbol to its file/line.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a fast, deterministic multi-language symbol index (definitions with file/line/kind) — the classic lightweight substrate for code navigation and repo maps.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: GPL-2.0-or-later, maintained successor to Exuberant Ctags. Aider's repo map and many code tools fall back to ctags-style tagging.

candidates.intent: Generate a call graph (who-calls-whom) for dynamic languages by parsing source into ASTs, finding function definitions, and connecting call sites.
candidates.input_contract: source files in Python, JavaScript, Ruby, or PHP
candidates.output_contract: a call graph (e.g. DOT/SVG) of function definitions and call edges
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot reliably build a complete call graph across files; it misses dynamic dispatch and call edges it cannot see in a limited context.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds AST-based definition discovery and call-site connection to emit a visual call graph, giving structural control-flow understanding of an unfamiliar repo.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: MIT, Python; supports Python/JS/Ruby/PHP. Call graphs for dynamic languages are heuristic (the README itself says 'pretty good'), so coverage < 1.0.

candidates.intent: Index a codebase and present an interactive graph + code + search view showing each symbol and its incoming/outgoing dependencies.
candidates.input_contract: a C/C++/Java/Python project (compilation database or project config)
candidates.output_contract: a navigable symbol-dependency graph linked to source locations
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot build or visualize a full symbol-dependency graph of an unfamiliar codebase or let a developer navigate it interactively.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deterministic indexer + interactive graph/code/search UI exposing per-symbol incoming/outgoing dependencies for fast onboarding to unfamiliar code.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: GPL-3.0 ('Sourcetrail' name is a Coati trademark, not GPL-covered); supports C/C++/Java/Python. ARCHIVED by maintainers end of 2021 — historical/reference candidate; the SourcetrailDB format lives on for custom indexers.

candidates.intent: Index a source tree to provide fast full-text search, symbol cross-references, and SCM-history-aware navigation across many languages.
candidates.input_contract: a source tree (optionally with SCM history) plus an index configuration
candidates.output_contract: a searchable, cross-referenced web view of the codebase with definition/reference links
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot index a large multi-repo source tree for instant cross-referenced search or reconcile it with SCM history.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deterministic source-search-and-cross-reference engine (definitions, references, history) for navigating large unfamiliar codebases.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + oracle.github.io/opengrok: license commonly CDDL-1.0 — confirm SPDX on repo LICENSE. Understands many file formats and SCM history.

candidates.intent: Search a codebase with combined neural semantic search, regex search, and precise code navigation in a local desktop app, with LLM reasoning over results.
candidates.input_contract: an indexed local repository plus a natural-language or regex query
candidates.output_contract: ranked code matches with navigation, plus LLM-synthesized answers about the code
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot index a repo for semantic+regex retrieval or navigate symbols precisely; it cannot ground answers in retrieved code beyond its context.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Rust-based neural semantic search (Qdrant) + regex + code navigation in one local app, with chained LLM calls to reason over retrieved code.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + Qdrant case study: BloopAI/bloop, Rust, fully open-source (commonly Apache-2.0 — confirm SPDX). YC S21. Semantic retrieval is deterministic given a model; the answer-synthesis step is LLM-dependent.

candidates.intent: Collect structured facts about code (definitions, references, types, call relationships) into a queryable database to answer 'where is X defined / what calls Y' across a large codebase.
candidates.input_contract: language-specific indexer output (facts) plus Angle queries
candidates.output_contract: query results over code facts (definitions, references, call edges, types)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot maintain a centralized, queryable fact base of code structure or answer precise cross-repo definition/reference/call questions reproducibly.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a scalable code-fact store with the Angle query language so tools/agents get exact structural answers (definitions, references, call graphs) instead of guessing.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: Meta's open-source code-indexing system (facebookincubator/Glean). Advanced for semantic queries but not turnkey — requires language indexers. Confirm SPDX (commonly BSD/MIT for Meta OSS) on the repo.

candidates.intent: Give a coding agent IDE-grade semantic code retrieval and editing at the symbol level (find symbol, find references, edit) over MCP, backed by language servers.
candidates.input_contract: a project plus symbol-level requests (find/edit/refactor) from an MCP client
candidates.output_contract: symbol definitions, references, and structured edits without reading whole files
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM reads whole files to understand structure, blowing its context window and missing precise references; it has no symbol graph or LSP semantics.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds an LSP-backed MCP toolkit so the agent explores at the symbol level (definitions/references/relationships) and edits surgically — IDE-grade understanding without full-file reads.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via repo fetch: MIT, Python ~90%, ~25k stars. Agent<->client layer is MCP; semantic analysis backend is language servers (LSP) by default (JetBrains plugin is a paid alternative). Symbol lookups are deterministic; agent orchestration is not.

candidates.intent: Add semantic code search to coding agents via an MCP server that does hybrid BM25 + dense-vector retrieval over an AST-chunked, embedded codebase.
candidates.input_contract: a codebase to index plus an embedding provider, a vector DB, and a search query
candidates.output_contract: relevant code snippets retrieved on demand instead of loading whole folders
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot make an entire codebase its context; it lacks an index and overflows its window when fed whole directories.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds AST-aware chunking + hybrid BM25+vector retrieval over Milvus/Zilliz with multiple embedding providers, cutting tokens ~40% while preserving retrieval quality.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via repo fetch: MIT, TypeScript 71.6%, AST chunking, embedding providers (OpenAI/VoyageAI/Ollama/Gemini), Milvus/Zilliz. By Zilliz (Milvus). Retrieval scoring is deterministic given a fixed model/index.

candidates.intent: Pre-index a codebase with tree-sitter into a local SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol/edge/file, served over MCP/CLI so agents answer structural questions without scanning files.
candidates.input_contract: a local codebase (auto re-indexed on file changes) plus structural queries (callers/callees/impact/definition/trace)
candidates.output_contract: structural query answers (definitions, signatures, callers, callees, impact, traces) from the pre-built graph
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM fans out across grep/glob/read to reconstruct how code fits together, burning tokens and tool calls and still missing edges.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a deterministic tree-sitter-derived symbol graph in local SQLite (no cloud, no embeddings, no code egress) with a file watcher and MCP/CLI/TS API — structural answers in a handful of calls.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: colbymchenry/codegraph, local-first, SQLite + tree-sitter, MCP-native (Claude Code/Cursor/Codex/etc.); extraction is AST-derived (deterministic), not LLM-summarized. Vendor+independent benchmarks ~59% fewer tokens / 70% fewer tool calls. Confirm SPDX on LICENSE.

candidates.intent: Index local code into a graph database and expose it as an MCP server + CLI to provide structural code context to AI assistants.
candidates.input_contract: a local codebase plus a graph-DB backend and context queries
candidates.output_contract: graph-structured code context (symbols, relationships) returned to an AI assistant via MCP
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no graph model of code relationships to query; it cannot answer cross-file structural questions reliably.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a code-to-graph indexer plus an MCP server/CLI so agents query a structural graph of the codebase for context.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: CodeGraphContext/CodeGraphContext, MCP server + CLI indexing local code into a graph DB. Distinct project from colbymchenry/codegraph. Confirm SPDX + the specific graph DB on the repo.

candidates.intent: Index a workspace with local embeddings + keyword search so an open-source IDE assistant can pull the most relevant files as @Codebase / @Folder context.
candidates.input_contract: a workspace plus an @Codebase/@Folder query and an embeddings model
candidates.output_contract: the most relevant files/snippets surfaced as context for the assistant
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot retrieve relevant files from a large workspace; without an index it can only see what is pasted into context.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds local embeddings (transformers.js, stored in ~/.continue/index) + keyword search and @Codebase/@Folder providers for repo-aware retrieval inside the IDE.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + docs: continuedev/continue, open-source IDE assistant (commonly Apache-2.0 — confirm SPDX). Default embeddings are local; the @Codebase provider is the in-scope indexing capability (it was being reworked/'deprecated' in docs — verify current provider name).

candidates.intent: Split source code into AST-aligned chunks (by tree-sitter nodes) for retrieval/embedding instead of naive fixed-size text splitting.
candidates.input_contract: a source-code document plus a language and chunk parameters
candidates.output_contract: AST-node-aligned code chunks as nodes/documents
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM (and naive splitters) chop code mid-function, destroying scope and producing low-quality embeddings/retrieval over a repo.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds tree-sitter-based splitting that keeps AST nodes intact, yielding semantically coherent code chunks for code RAG.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: CodeSplitter in run-llama/llama_index, MIT, splits by AST nodes via tree-sitter. The chunking is deterministic; downstream embedding/retrieval is model-dependent.

candidates.intent: Build a navigable hierarchy of all code scopes in a directory (function/class/method) where scope bodies are replaced with pointers, so an LLM can traverse parents/children on demand.
candidates.input_contract: a code directory plus a language grammar
candidates.output_contract: a scope hierarchy of linked nodes (parent/child) with bodies elided into 'search this node' references
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot fit a large repo in context; reading whole files to find one scope wastes the window and loses the structural map.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a tree-sitter scope hierarchy with elided bodies and parent/child links, letting an agent traverse the codebase structure and fetch only the scope it needs.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: llama-index-packs-code-hierarchy (CodeHierarchyNodeParser), MIT, tree-sitter-based. A LlamaPack (skills-pack-style); the hierarchy construction is deterministic, traversal is agent-driven.

candidates.intent: Search code across public GitHub repositories via the REST API to locate symbols, files, and usage by query, language, repo, or path qualifiers.
candidates.input_contract: a search query (q) plus optional repo/org/language/path filters and an auth token
candidates.output_contract: matching code results with repo/path/line metadata (and optional text-match highlights)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot query GitHub's live code index; it cannot find where a symbol is used across public repos or retrieve current file contents.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds programmatic access to GitHub's code index (language-analyzer-backed) so an agent finds real definitions/usages across millions of public repos with source handles.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via GitHub Docs: GET /search/code, authenticated, ~9 req/min, legacy syntax (no new path: qualifier). It is a hosted API (not OSS) — SPDX 'unknown' / terms-of-service governed. Ranking has some opacity, hence ceiling < 1.0.

candidates.intent: Perform structural search-and-replace across ~every language using lightweight syntax-aware match templates (balanced delimiters, holes) rather than regex.
candidates.input_contract: a match template + rewrite template plus a target codebase
candidates.output_contract: structurally matched regions and their rewrites (diffs)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot reliably match nested/balanced syntactic structures or apply consistent rewrites at scale; regex breaks on real code.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds language-agnostic structural matching (delimiter-aware templates with holes) and deterministic rewrites for understanding and transforming code patterns.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: comby-tools/comby, Apache-2.0 (per comby.opam), OCaml. comby.dev. In-scope as a precise structural code-query/rewrite engine.

candidates.intent: Produce a language-agnostic index of a codebase (definitions, references, implementations, documentation) in the SCIP format to power go-to-definition/find-references for tools and agents.
candidates.input_contract: a codebase processed by a SCIP indexer for the language
candidates.output_contract: a SCIP index (protobuf) of symbols with definitions, references, implementations, and hover docs
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no precise, language-agnostic symbol index; it cannot resolve definitions/references across files reliably or interoperably.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a compact, efficient successor to LSIF: a portable code-intelligence index (definitions/references/implementations/docs) that many tools can produce and consume.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: sourcegraph/scip (SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol), commonly Apache-2.0 — confirm SPDX. Replaced LSIF; per-language indexers (scip-python, scip-typescript, etc.) produce the index that powers Sourcegraph navigation.

candidates.intent: Index code locally and run a server over indexed repos, using VoyageAI embeddings for semantic search plus full-text search and git-log indexing, with experimental SCIP support.
candidates.input_contract: a local repository plus an embedding key and a search query
candidates.output_contract: semantic + full-text search results over the indexed repo for AI-optimized navigation
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot index a repo for semantic retrieval or search git history; it lacks any persistent local index.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds local code indexing with VoyageAI embeddings, FTS, git-log indexing, and experimental SCIP, exposing AI-optimized semantic code navigation over a server.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search (GitHub topic lsif-indexer): jsbattig/code-indexer, Python; uses VoyageAI embeddings + FTS + experimental SCIP. Confirm SPDX on the repo. Retrieval is deterministic given a fixed model/index.

candidates.intent: Produce a tree-sitter ranked map of a git repository (the Aider repo-map mechanism extracted as a standalone tool/MCP server).
candidates.input_contract: a git repository plus a token budget
candidates.output_contract: a ranked repo map of key symbols/files with locations, sized to a token budget
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no symbol-ranked map to pick high-signal context from a large repo and overflows its window when fed everything.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds Aider's tree-sitter + ranking repo-map as a reusable tool/MCP server so any agent can request a compact, ranked structural map of an unfamiliar codebase.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search (mcpservers.org + repo): pdavis68/RepoMapper, based entirely on Aider.chat's Repo Map. Confirm SPDX on LICENSE. The map computation is deterministic (tree-sitter + graph ranking).

candidates.intent: Turn any public GitHub repo into a chat-queryable subject-matter expert to locate functionality, understand code, debug, and decide where changes go.
candidates.input_contract: a GitHub repo URL plus natural-language questions about the codebase
candidates.output_contract: natural-language answers pinpointing where functionality lives and where changes should be made, grounded in the repo
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM has no access to an arbitrary repo's full contents and cannot reliably answer 'where is X' across an unfamiliar codebase.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds repo ingestion + retrieval so the model answers grounded questions about any public repo (locate functionality, debug, plan changes).
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + Product Hunt: hosted SaaS (getonboard.dev), YC W24, free for public repos under 100MB. NOT open-source / no public repo confirmed — source_kind approximated as a tool; SPDX 'unknown', ToS-governed. Answers are LLM-generated over retrieval (low determinism).

candidates.intent: Build a semantic graph of an entire repository to answer codebase Q&A and do cross-file/cross-service impact analysis.
candidates.input_contract: a connected repository plus natural-language questions or impact queries
candidates.output_contract: answers about the codebase and cross-file impact analysis grounded in the repo graph
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot index a whole repo into a graph or reason about cross-file/cross-service impact beyond its context window.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a semantic repo graph enabling deep codebase Q&A and impact analysis across files and services.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search (Ry Walker code-intelligence comparison + Sourcegraph-alternative listings): hosted SaaS, no public OSS repo confirmed. SPDX 'unknown', ToS-governed. Q&A is LLM-generated; included for completeness as a repo-comprehension peer.

candidates.intent: Use a code search API to pull context (symbols, APIs, usage patterns) from local and remote codebases so an AI assistant can understand, write, and fix code across an entire codebase.
candidates.input_contract: connected local/remote repositories plus a query or coding request
candidates.output_contract: codebase context (relevant symbols/files/usages) surfaced to the assistant, with answers/edits grounded in it
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot search a large or remote codebase for relevant symbols/usages; it has no cross-repo code-search infrastructure.

candidates.intent: Run CodeQL-style queries over a codebase using tree-sitter infrastructure (a lightweight CodeQL alternative for structural code search).
candidates.input_contract: CodeQL-like queries plus a target codebase parsed by tree-sitter
candidates.output_contract: query results identifying code matching the structural/semantic query
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot run reproducible structural/semantic queries over code or guarantee it found every match.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Adds a CodeQL-query interface backed by tree-sitter, giving lightweight, deterministic structural code search without CodeQL's heavyweight database build.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: travitch/ql-grep, 'implements CodeQL on the tree-sitter infrastructure'. Confirm SPDX + language coverage on the repo before relying.
